_what: The answer to every readback tools/gen_notify_readback.py finds. R3b says a notify scope may not write state that translated libmh reads back in the same frame -- under a NULL-callback host the dispatch defers to frame edge and libmh reads LAST frame's value. The generator finds candidates mechanically; this file says what each one actually is.
_why_a_list_and_not_a_rule: The intersection cannot see frame ORDER. A reader that provably always runs before the emit is harmless, and no closure over a call graph can tell you that -- somebody has to read the frame body and say so. Same shape as tools/data/rebind_yield_dispositions.json: the gate refuses anything unlisted, and every entry carries the reason that made it acceptable.
_history: The sweep this ledger came out of was itself a missed check. R3b was written at LIFT-TACT slice 0 (e2e6907c, 22:48) and the on_screen scopes had landed 49-71 minutes EARLIER; nothing ran the new rule backwards over them. The 2026-09-04 hand sweep found 8 readbacks over 42 scopes, one severe (INV_TACT_SIDEBAR_ROSTER). This file plus the generator is what stops the next rule arriving after the next scope.

_frame_cuts.llm_strat_frame_sim_only: The game's own frame driver. Several screen scopes reach it (a modal that pumps the frame), and past it the closure saturates at 775 functions -- the whole reachable program. Those writes belong to the FRAME, not to the scope that opened the modal, so the walk stops here and records that it crossed. WITHOUT this cut, outcome_dialog / overlay_dismiss / bldg_panel_open / planet_select_open / sync_overlay_show / wait_player_show / mp_leave_reset / progress_notify all report 775 reachable and 'writes everything', which is true and useless.

_frame_cuts_rejected.game_SetEvent: MEASURED and REJECTED 2026-09-09. Cutting here collapses llm_ui_bldg_panel_open 50 -> 1 and llm_progress_notify_unit_available 50 -> 1, which is exactly why it is tempting and exactly why it is wrong: game_SetEvent is the game's EVENT DISPATCHER, not a frame loop. A scope that fires a game event genuinely causes that event's writes, and hiding them behind a cut would be tuning the cut set until the report is short. Only a re-entry into the frame loop qualifies as a cut.

_verdicts.fixed: The readback no longer reaches libmh -- the write was hoisted above the emit, or the value is now computed by libmh itself. The entry stays so the gate does not re-open it.
_verdicts.required-class: The entry is NOT converted to a notify record; it stays a required host-table call, dispatched synchronously by contract. R3's own escape hatch.
_verdicts.justified-exempt: The intersection is real but harmless, for a reason the closure cannot see -- the reader provably precedes the emit, the read is a dead store, or the region is not consumed for any decision. The reason must say WHICH.
_verdicts.over-approximation: The pair exists only because the closure over-reaches past a frame cut or through a shared leaf; the scope's own subtree does not write it on any live path.
_verdicts.handed-off: The readback is real and the FIX belongs to another tracker item, named in the reason. Distinct from justified-exempt: nothing here argues it is harmless -- it argues it is someone else's slice. The gate stays green only because the owning item exists and is open.

_how_to_add: Run `python tools/gen_notify_readback.py --md` for the worklist, read the actual frame body, then add a pairs[] entry {kind, region, verdict, reason} or, for a crossed/blind scope, a scopes[] entry {kind, verdict, reason}. A reason that only cites a rule is not a reason -- cite the code.

pairs.reason: HOISTED 2026-09-09. mh::state::evt::cam_set_col now writes RID_MAP_CAM_COL itself before emitting (state/host_events.cpp), so llm_strat_spawn_enemy_landing's hashed landing_x fallback (sim_landing_spot.cpp:147-150) reads a value libmh owns rather than one the host may not have applied yet. The double write is idempotent BY MEASUREMENT: llm_map_cam_set_col @0x0044af33 is `mov [0x00e58138],eax` verbatim -- no clamp, no transform -- then derives SCROLL_OFFSET_COL = col<<5, and no translated body reads that derived value (zero hits for CAM_SCROLL_OFFSET across src/mh_dll).
Row half of the CAM_SET_COL hoist, same shape and same measurement (llm_map_cam_set_row @0x0044af6d). See that entry for the evidence.

DEAD READ, and the source says so in as many words: the only translated consumer is sim_fx_debris_burst.cpp:83, `(void)c.zoom_scale_x_get();`, whose own comment keeps the call solely for the original's internal state-read and discards the value. Nothing branches on the zoom scale, so a frame-stale value changes nothing.

FIXED 2026-09-09 at LIFT-TACT slice A -- the SEVERE finding, and the only one of LIFT-R3B's eight that needed code rather than a reason. llm_tact_ui_sidebar_roster_refresh @0x00434b68 is an R2 split that shipped unsplit: three STATE steps (rebuild the visible-slot list from live tact_units, clamp sidebar_slot_scroll, set the four sel_panel_icon_slot_state arrow bits) and then a redraw loop. llm_tact_sidebar_dispatch reads ALL THREE back later in the same frame -- slot ids at tact_sidebar_dispatch.cpp:144/153, icon slot state at :130 -- and turns a slot id into a hashed tact_units.status write. libmh now computes the state half itself in detail::roster_slots_rebuild(), above the emit (tact_selection_panel_refresh.cpp); the scope keeps only the draw. The double write is idempotent by construction: steps 1-3 are a pure function of tact_units + sidebar_slot_visible_count and nothing between the hoist and the host's execution touches either. Pinned by tacttest T5a/T5b/T5c and MUTATION-PROVEN -- deleting the tail zero-fill turns T5a red with the stale poison value still in the slot map.

Fixed by the same roster_slots_rebuild hoist as TACT_SIDEBAR_SLOT_UNIT_IDS -- the scroll clamp is its second state step (@0x00434bc9-0x00434bf5), computed in libmh above the emit and pinned by tacttest T5b. See that entry for the derivation.

ELEMENT-DISJOINT, which a region-granular intersection cannot see. NOT CONSUMED FOR A DECISION. llm_strat_render_tile_object @0x0045229a increments strat_soldiers[].anim_change_count per render; the reader, sim_unit_soldier_screen_pos.cpp:67, folds it into a walk-cycle SPRITE FRAME used only to place a muzzle flash or an unload sprite (sim_unit_fire_weapon.cpp, sim_unit_transport_unload.cpp). IDEMPOTENT COPY OF A SESSION-STABLE SOURCE. llm_gfx_draw_cursor_menu @0x004a5b74 stores G_WIN_H = WindowHeight, and WindowHeight is written only at boot and at explicit resolution-change entry points, never per frame. Deferring the copy by a frame cannot change its value, because the source does not move between the two instants.

Same idempotent-copy argument as G_WIN_H (@0x004a5b6f), plus mode exclusivity: the two extra readers (llm_tact_cam_follow_selection_tick, llm_tact_camera_center_on_tile) are tactical-only, reached solely via llm_frame_dispatch case 6, while this scope's only translated emit site is gated on own.game_mode()==3 (sim_tutorial_step_driver.cpp:308-309). DESTINATION-ONLY, and mode-exclusive besides. _G_LLM_FRAMEBUFFER is a POINTER to the locked back buffer that llm_gfx_present_flip @0x0042644a re-caches after its unlock/present/lock cycle; all five readers use own.gfx_framebuffer() purely as the destination address of a memmove/blit (tact_view_shift.cpp:55,102,148,193; tact_mission_start.cpp:151), never as a branch input. The readers are tactical-mode; both emit sites (sim_tutorial_step_driver.cpp:310, sim_start_tutorial.cpp:67) are strategic/tutorial.

Same writer and same argument as SCR_PRESENT_FLIP: the fade tick reaches llm_gfx_present_flip -> llm_gfx_surface_lock on every step, and FRAMEBUFFER's readers are tactical-only while this scope's only emit site (sim_start_tutorial.cpp:60,162) is strategic session setup.

CORRECTED 2026-09-09, same day it was written -- the first reason was too strong and a determinism run disproved it. It said the readback was 'pacing, not determinism (R8)'. FIXED 2026-09-09 by draining in libmh. The hazardous site was sim_fx_debris_burst.cpp:33, which emitted the clear and THEN refilled the queue the host was being asked to drain (offsets 46-62, count :77) -- under poll the deferred drain would have consumed the burst libmh had just queued, a different action rather than a stale read. libmh now performs llm_cam_jump_queue_pop @0x0044dd43's loop itself, crossing the channel through the existing kinds so the hosted arm makes the same original calls in the same order (R5). The two remaining emit sites keep the record and are safe by MEASUREMENT, not assumption: llm_strat_session_state_reset and llm_game_load do not refill afterwards, and neither is reachable from llm_strat_frame, so neither can share a frame with the camera readback.

NO READER RUNS BETWEEN THIS EMIT AND THE END OF ITS BRANCH -- measured, not argued. The scope's one site is llm_tact_frame's mine-blast exit branch (tact_frame.cpp:140), and everything libmh does after it before the branch returns is blink_overlay_clear, vis_map_fill_default, units_reset_hp_for_active, squad_sync_hp, scroll_target_proximity_tick and mission_end_return_to_strategic -- grepped, and between them they contain ZERO references to gfx_framebuffer or the window metrics. The closure's readers (view_shift x4, mission_start) are reached on other frames entirely. Deferring the whole wipe to the frame edge therefore cannot be observed by libmh on this path.

Same no-reader-after-the-emit measurement as FRAMEBUFFER above, AND the idempotent-copy argument SCR_CURSOR_MENU_DRAW already carries for this region: the write is llm_gfx_draw_cursor_ingame copying WindowWidth into G_WIN_W, and WindowWidth moves only at boot and at explicit resolution-change entry points, never per frame. A deferred copy of a source that does not move between the two instants stores the same value.

DESTINATION-ONLY, and the one site where it is NOT terminal is named rather than glossed. Two emit sites: llm_tact_frame's last statement (tact_frame.cpp:475), where nothing of libmh's runs afterwards at all, and llm_tact_mission_start step 2 (tact_mission_start.cpp:70), which DOES read own.gfx_framebuffer() later in the same call, at :151. That second one is a genuine same-call readback and it is exempt on what the value IS, not on ordering: _G_LLM_FRAMEBUFFER is the address of the locked back buffer, and :151 uses it purely as the destination of a 480-row memcpy -- never as a branch input, never hashed, not a TACT_HASH_REGIONS member. A stale pointer there lands the intro blit on the surface that is about to be presented rather than the one after it: one frame of presentation, and by R8 it cannot reach the sim. The same destination-only reading already exempts SCR_PRESENT_FLIP and SCR_FADE_TRANSITION_RUN for this region; what does NOT carry over is their second leg, mode exclusivity, since this scope and its readers are both tactical.

IDEMPOTENT COPY OF A SESSION-STABLE SOURCE, the same argument SCR_CURSOR_MENU_DRAW carries: llm_gfx_draw_cursor_ingame stores G_WIN_W = WindowWidth, and WindowWidth is written only at boot and at explicit resolution-change entry points, never per frame. Deferring the copy by a frame cannot change its value because the source does not move between the two instants. Mode exclusivity is NOT claimed here -- this scope and its readers are both tactical -- so the idempotence is doing all the work.

MISSION-BOUNDARY ONE-SHOT: EVERY READER IS IN A LATER FRAME, and the emitter reads none of it. Measured both halves. (1) Structure: llm_tact_mission_start is reached ONLY from llm_strat_try_enter_tactical_mission and llm_tact_mission_end_return_to_strategic only from llm_tact_frame's mission-end branch (committed call graph), while every reader below is reached only from a later frame's llm_tact_frame / llm_strat_frame. A frame-edge drain therefore lands before any of them runs -- which is the ordering fact the gate says it cannot see, and the reason this ledger exists rather than the gate deciding. (2) Self-read: the emitting body reads NOTHING it emits after the emit -- mission_start's only window_width read is at :116-117, BEFORE the emits; view_tiles_w/h at :133-134 are writes, not reads; and it never mentions sprite_pix_offsets, tile_vis_map_ptr, los_cache or gfx_panel_row_skip at all. mission_end mentions none of them. Contrast the two entries this slice REVERTED: llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution and llm_gfx_apply_resolution_change failed exactly this second check and stayed required. NOTE this pair was a REAL same-call readback until earlier the same day: llm_tact_ui_sel_panel_init read it three times inside mission_start's own call chain, and slice A moved that draw head host-side. The region now has ZERO translated readers -- all five remaining references are in mh.dll's sink. The gate still lists the original-graph readers, which is why the pair needs a row rather than disappearing.
